description: Systemic (E2): what is true across the whole portfolio? The only rulebook whose questions cannot be asked of one submission — each rule is a sweep across every dossier on the ledger, computable from evidence already filed. Its dials lived as Python defaults until now, which meant the one supervisory layer a regulator could not tune was the market-level one.

rules.description: One payee takes a disproportionate share of spend at operators with nothing to do with each other, and arrived recently. Three conditions together, because any one alone is ordinary: most counterparties are shared, because popular retailers are popular.
rules.notes: min_share separates narrow-and-deep from broad-and-shallow; recent_days separates an incumbent that grew into a large share over years from one that arrived last month.

rules.description: No single model version is behind more than max_share of the agents on the register. Not a defect in any operator — each independently picked a good model — the risk is emergent: one provider incident becomes a correlated failure across the whole population.
rules.notes: The finding most likely to be trivially true in a small corpus, which is worth saying out loud rather than letting a demo imply otherwise. Sweep it before trusting the dial.

rules.description: Agents at unrelated firms are not moving together. Correlated behaviour amplifies market stress — agents on similar models emphasise the same signals and make the same errors under pressure — so tight correlation means an undeclared shared trigger, a real market event, or a common compromise.
rules.notes: max_correlation is ASSERTED, not proven. Measured over the span two agents actually share, pairwise daily-count correlation across the four corpus dossiers runs -0.34 to +0.06, and two of the six pairs have too little overlap to measure at all, so 0.7 leaves headroom — but four agents is a small population and daily counts are sparse. This is the dial most in need of a sandbox sweep before it binds anyone. min_overlap_days exists because a correlation over a fortnight is arithmetic, not evidence.

rules.description: The same retrieved content, already flagged as carrying an injected instruction, does not appear at several unrelated operators. Firm by firm it looks like an incident; across the portfolio it is a campaign.
rules.notes: result_digest earns its place here: the hash cannot reveal that content carries an injection — only reading the text does — but once one firm's excerpt has been read, the same digest elsewhere identifies the same payload without anyone reading it twice.
